the acetylation of PA and sulphaguanidine is not affected by adjuvant treatment in male rats and the NAPA percentage is increased in the urine of adjuvant-treated rats, whereas the NAPA percentage of PA and sulphamethazine was decreased in adjuvant treated rats.

a study of the influence of PA and sulphamethizole on the metabolism of sulphadimine in rats.
the effects of adjuvant treatment on the metabolism of sulphadimide and PA in male rats.
the effects of adjuvant arthritis and PA on the acetylation of sulphadimide and PA in rats.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
PA and sulphadidimidine are metabolized by the same enzyme systems.
the metabolism of PA in the rat was not affected by the adjuvant treatment, whereas the metabolism of sulphadimide in adjuvant treated rats differed markedly from that of the untreated controls.

the metabolism of PA in man and rats is different from that of sulphadimide.
the acetylated metabolite of PA is formed in the rat in the same manner as that of sulphadimide, i.e. by acetylation of the parent compound.
the metabolism of PA in the male rat is different to that of the female and that of the male and female guinea-pig.
